headline: High-risk write/egress pair: Plandex can modify local files and use broad network egress, while awesome-python is a non-runnable docs-only collection with no protective runtime surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runtime or I/O surfaces, so it cannot ingest B’s outputs directly. B can read/write project files and stdout/stderr, so only a manual copy-paste or file bridge could carry injected content into B. That makes the pathway possible but unusual, with limited blast radius.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-generated text into B’s prompt or files, injection becomes possible.
IF B is configured to parse untrusted file content as instructions, the risk materializes.
mitigations: Keep A as a read-only reference source.
Do not paste A-derived text into B without review.
Use a separate notes file for human review only.
Disable any auto-apply or auto-ingest workflow in B.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between tools.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no execution surface, so it cannot leak data itself. B touches source code and has broad network egress, but the pair only becomes a leakage path if sensitive files are placed in B’s workspace. The blast radius is limited to whatever the operator loads into B.
conditions: IF sensitive files are opened inside B’s project directory, B can transmit them over network egress.
IF the operator keeps sensitive data out of B’s workspace, this risk does not materialize.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in B’s project directory.
Use a scrubbed sample repo for testing.
Review outbound requests before enabling network access.
Rotate any secrets accidentally exposed to B.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data loss prevention.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or execution capability, but B can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses in a shared project directory. Because B’s concurrency model includes shared state via the Plandex backend, overlapping writes can conflict if multiple instances or humans touch the same repo. A is not a writer, so it is not the conflict source.
conditions: IF two B instances or a human editor modify the same repo concurrently, write conflicts can occur.
IF the project directory is shared across sessions, B can overwrite staged changes.
mitigations: Use one writer per repo at a time.
Pause other editors before applying B changes.
Commit or stash before starting a new B session.
Review staged diffs before apply.
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared workspaces.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a static collection, so it cannot generate authoritative facts. B can act on prompts and modify code, and its review-then-apply flow can still propagate mistaken instructions if the operator treats A’s curated links as authoritative context. The pathway exists only through human mediation, so it is not high.
conditions: IF the operator uses A’s curated links as factual authority for B’s plan, B may act on incorrect assumptions.
IF B auto-applies changes derived from unverified guidance, errors can cascade into code changes.
mitigations: Verify claims from A against primary sources.
Keep B in review-only mode for first pass.
Require human approval before apply.
Compare B’s plan against repository tests.
requires-engineering: add citation checks before apply.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class or residency mismatch is evidenced. A is a docs-only open-source collection with no data handling, and B’s touched data class is source code, not PHI or regulated personal data. The pair does not show a residency or certification conflict in the profiles.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is introduced into B’s workspace, a separate compliance review is required.
IF A remains a static documentation source, no compliance pathway appears.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B’s workspace.
Use non-sensitive sample code for evaluation.
Document data-class boundaries for the workflow.
